spec: Phone hero order: headline, sub, action, then one real object at full column width with its top 100 to 200px showing above the fold. 16 to 24px gutters, 36 to 48px headline on two to four lines. The cut edge says keep scrolling. The safe default for product pages.

Art leaves the side column and moves above the headline: a 300 to 340px object, then a 36 to 48px centred title, copy and action, all on one screen. Flip with CSS order so the source stays headline first. Use when the picture explains faster than the sentence.

The form is the hero on phones. Heading 36 to 54px on up to three lines, then 48px full-width fields set at 16px so iOS never zooms. Email and button may share a row. Secondary art moves below. For sign-up, booking, donation and search.

Full-bleed portrait photo or film at 84 to 100svh. Copy pinned low left at a 16 to 24px margin: 36 to 48px heading, one line, 44 to 52px button in thumb reach. Scrim only behind the text. Stop short of the fold so the next band peeks in.

The hero stays an object: a panel inset 8 to 20px from the viewport, radius 16 to 32, 76 to 94 percent of screen height. Copy centred or anchored low, buttons near its base. Margin and radius hold at every width. Only padding and type change.

Product window kept whole at 50 to 60 percent scale, left edge near the gutter, cut by the right edge and the fold, dimming away from the left. Show one focused document with three type sizes, not a table. Structure must read, words need not.

A centred object 230 to 260px wide with companions cropped by both screen edges, 40 to 65px showing each side. Make the stage wider than the phone, about 520px, and centre it with translateX. Reads as a wider world, not a squeezed row. For hardware, apps and auth.

Signature art survives by being cropped, not shrunk. A disc sized past the viewport leaves two arcs, a ribbon retreats into one corner, a mascot tucks top right, a glyph sits behind the headline at 320px. Size in vw, keep it out of the text zone, clip the section.

Drop the big window and put one small real moment in its slot: a 236 to 340px card with one prompt, one chart or one notification, on a glow or tinted plate, between hairlines. Never a shrunken full screen. It reads at phone size and loads faster.

The whole composition scales down unchanged: render, lockup and labels keep their positions at about 90 percent width. Only for stages with no small text, such as 3D renders, film and big lockups. Do not use it for interfaces, where 12px text turns to 5px.

The image is recut for portrait, not letterboxed. Serve a separate tall crop with picture and media at 700px, or set object-position per breakpoint. Crop tighter on the subject, 680 to 800px tall. Text moves into the space the new crop leaves open.

Same pieces, new arrangement, placed by hand for 390 by 844: robots fall into a diagonal, a wall of photos drops to two lanes, a diptych merges into one panel, title mid-screen, action low. Highest craft and highest cost. Worth it on one hero only.

When art only decorates, cut it. Keep headline, proof and action, raise the type one step, and let a hairline or the next section do the pacing. No illustration beats a 120px thumbnail of one. For text-strong docs and developer pages.

Swap what a phone cannot do for what it can. A desktop download becomes a disabled 42px pill pointing to a desktop, above a live sign-up button, or a button pair becomes an email field that sends a demo link. State the swap in plain words.

Buttons fill the column and stack: 44 to 56px tall, 8 to 16px apart, primary filled, secondary outlined, a trust line or text link beneath. Best for a single-goal conversion page. Only about 3 in 10 gold heroes do this, so treat it as a choice, not a rule.

Two buttons share one row, equal halves or inline, 40 to 48px tall, 8px gap, labels under 16 characters. Both actions land in one glance and it saves 56px of height. Test the longer label at 360px wide, and stack only if it wraps.

The button keeps its own width and holds the left edge: 44 to 54px tall, hugging the label, two stacked left if needed. Reads calmer and more premium than a full bar. The most common choice on gold sites. Best with strong imagery or a serif.

Fixed action at the foot, phones only, 56 to 72px tall with safe-area padding, opaque ground, top hairline. Either a pill plus text link, or one bar inset 12 to 16px. Reveal it once the hero CTA leaves the screen, and reserve matching page padding.

Keep two columns instead of one: tiles 165 to 188px wide, 4 to 12px gaps, square or 5:6, gutter down to 5 to 16px. Twice the density, more choice per screen, no carousel. Labels must fit 150px. For shops, categories, galleries and teams.

A collection becomes a sideways rail: cards 230 to 345px wide, 12px gap, next card showing 30 to 65px at the edge, scroll-snap to start, padding and scroll-padding equal to the gutter, scrollbar hidden. Any arrows 40 to 44px. For products, cases and events.

Grid falls to one column with the card anatomy unchanged: same radius, padding one step less, 12 to 16px gaps, full column width. Fixed heights go. Inner media stays at desktop size and is cropped by the card. Tile order follows reading order.

Cards dissolve into a ruled list: one column, 1px rules, each entry repeating one rhythm of meta, media, title and dek. Dates in side rails fold to a small line above the title. 24 to 34px after each rule. For news, changelogs, catalogues and directories.

One picture per row at column width, with the caption moved off the image to the page ground: 16 to 20px title, 12px caps meta, 30 to 40px to the next picture. At 2:1 three pictures fit a screen. For portfolios, architecture and galleries.

Metrics keep every value but fold to two columns, 2x2 or 2x3, in one panel with a 1px rule between columns and no boxes. Three across works if labels fit 110px. Numbers 20 to 28px tabular. Charts keep their axes at 280 to 300px tall.

A filter sidebar collapses to one control: a 36 to 50px icon chip, one open-filters button beside sort, or a two-column list of bare heads. Results move up so the first thumbnail shows on screen one. Keep the active filter count visible.

A wide compare table shows one plan at a time: name, price and a full-width button flanked by 36px previous and next arrows, pinned on scroll. Feature groups collapse, rows 53px, single column. No sideways scroll and no squeezed columns.

Plans stack one per screen at 16 to 24px gutters, 8 to 24px gaps, CTA full width in each card, billing toggle centred above and pinned if long. Collapse the free plan to one row, name left and price right, so the paid plan arrives sooner.

Plan columns survive as a sideways rail: 250px columns split by hairlines, next plan peeking at the edge, tile, button and list intact. Keeps plans comparable where a stack does not. Shorten tab labels to fit. Best with three to five plans and short lists.

Rank the columns. Keep the name and one key value, and move the rest to a 13px second line inside the name cell, or drop them. Never scroll the whole table. Rows 56 to 64px tall, tabular figures, right-aligned value, 1px rules.

Code never wraps and never shrinks under 13px. Keep 13 to 15px mono, line numbers and filename tab, and clip at the card edge or run the card off the right, with overflow-x auto inside the block. Install commands truncate but keep the copy button.

A long tab strip collapses to one control: a full-width 44 to 48px native select, or a centred label with left and right chevrons. Every option stays reachable and nothing clips. Use a select past four options or for long labels.

Exposed page rails survive by moving out to the gutter: verticals 16 to 24px from each edge, horizontal rules snapping on, nodes kept, cards inset inside them. The rails are the identity, so never drop them for space. For developer and finance pages.

A ruled grid stacks to full-width rows. Horizontal rules stay, vertical rules go, adjacent cells share one border so no line doubles. Labels move above their content, 16 to 24px padding. The grid logic survives with no cards added.

Keep the desktop stagger inside one column: a picture indented 50px, a photo running off one edge with a caption card crossing its corner, or two offset lanes. Insets of 12 to 50px are enough. Beats a centred stack for editorial and brand pages.

Design it as a document and the phone needs almost nothing: same type scale, same chrome, one column, 16 to 24px gutters, no restyle. Body stays 14 to 19px. Best for essays, manifestos, portfolios and strict systems where the voice is the design.

The headline stays huge because it is the design: 17vw sets about 66px on a 390 screen, two to four short lines, tracking -.03em, left or offset. Size it from the longest word and break lines by hand. Only for short phrases.

The wordmark is refit to span the phone, gutter to gutter, about 350px wide, breaking into two rows or stacking letters if needed. Crop an SVG viewBox to the ink so it scales without distortion. Height follows the word. One bold gesture on the first screen.

56 to 64px bar: logo left, one compact action and a menu glyph right, all on one centre line, 16 to 24px gutters. The action is 32 to 40px tall, pill or tile matching the page. Sign-up stays visible and everything else goes behind the menu. Default for products.

Logo and one thin glyph, nothing else: two 18 to 24px hairlines 6 to 8px apart, stroke matching the logo weight, no button shape, 20px margins, no bar fill. Hit area still 44px. Works over photographs and for calm brands.

The menu glyph sits on its own ground: a 36 to 44px square, circle or pill in tint, brand fill or outline, matching the site's button shape. Gives an icon an edge on busy art. A 92 by 46px flush block is the bold form.

No icon: the word Menu set in the site's own link or label style, 13 to 20px, plain or underlined, opposite the mark. Reads as written, not stock. Pad to a 44px hit area. For studios, editorial and type-led sites with no chrome.

Replace the three bars with a glyph from the brand: a descending funnel for a filterable archive, a thin plus, a four-dot grid, lines of unequal length. Same 24px box, same stroke as the logo. One small owned detail beats a redesigned bar.

If three or four links fit at 14 to 16px, show them and drop the menu: a 358px tray spaced evenly, corner links at 16px inset, or inline links under the name. Desktop and phone share one object. Only for sites with under five destinations.

Commerce bar: menu left, mark centred or left, then 20 to 24px line icons for search, account and bag at 44px pitch. A 1fr auto 1fr grid keeps the mark centred whatever each side holds. The count sits in the bag.

A 45px bar split by hairlines into 45px square cells: menu and search left, account and bag right, empty centre until the wordmark docks on scroll. 14 to 16px line icons, no labels. Rigid and fashion-like. A strict grid the rest of the page repeats.

The bar as a floating card: inset 8 to 20px, 56 to 66px tall, radius 16 to 100, white or blurred fill, soft shadow, logo left, menu tile right. The page wash shows in the gutters, so the hero reads as running behind it. Sticky 12px from the top.

The bar stays empty of logo while the hero shows it large. Once scrolled, a 16 to 24px mark docks into the bar, left or centre. Avoids two logos on one screen. Use with a big wordmark hero and a 150 to 200ms fade.

Search is the nav: a 42 to 54px field fills the bar beside a menu icon and account, or stays pinned full width under the header. Links go behind the menu. For marketplaces, directories and catalogues, where people arrive knowing what they want.

For local services: under the logo, a row of actions that do something at once, such as call, email, directions and menu, as 32 to 44px icon buttons with 11px labels, or one split block for Menu and Ask. Real tel and mailto links, not forms.

App-style tabs for sites people use rather than read: three to five icon-and-label items, 24 to 28px icons, 10 to 11px labels, 56 to 64px tall plus safe area, opaque, top hairline or rounded top. One active colour. Never on a marketing page.

The site nav moves to the foot: a 60px bar with mark left and three or four 32px framed icon buttons right, or a darker 40px search strip above a row of 16px links. The top of the page stays free. For docs and developer sites.

A floating dock instead of a bar: a 52px capsule inset 16px from edges and base, name left, one high-contrast Menu pill right, or a 54px menu circle beside a 245px CTA pill, or one 46px button alone. Thumb reach, no top bar needed.

The docs sidebar becomes a 44 to 48px sticky bottom bar: section icon, current section, chevron. A tap raises the same tree as a sheet capped at 60svh, with the current page tinted and a scrim behind. Location stays visible and within thumb reach.

Two stacked sticky rows in docs: a 56px identity row with logo, version, search and overflow, then a 40 to 56px row with menu glyph and breadcrumb ending in the current page. The sidebar hides and the location stays. Truncate the path, never the page name.

A row under the header that scrolls sideways and clips at the screen edge: 11 to 14px links or chips, or 60px round photos with 12px labels, cut through the fifth item. Pin the section name at left. Fade only the right end.
